claim.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve

roles.L0/N1877+: Layer-0 count-word neuron: fires on ' seven' and ' twelve' and nowhere else in the prompt (1.99 and 2.55). It marks both count slots, so the key after ' seven' and the query at ' twelve' share a 'count word' feature for the copy heads to match.
roles.L0/N1277+: Layer-0 count-word neuron: fires on ' seven' and ' twelve' and nowhere else in the prompt (0.87 and 1.15). It marks both count slots, so the key after ' seven' and the query at ' twelve' share a 'count word' feature for the copy heads to match.
roles.L0/N1108+: Layer-0 count-word neuron: fires on ' seven' and ' twelve' and nowhere else in the prompt (2.41 and 2.25). It marks both count slots, so the key after ' seven' and the query at ' twelve' share a 'count word' feature for the copy heads to match.
roles.L0/N141+: Layer-0 count-word neuron: fires on ' seven' and ' twelve' and nowhere else in the prompt (1.23 and 0.93). It marks both count slots, so the key after ' seven' and the query at ' twelve' share a 'count word' feature for the copy heads to match.
roles.L0/N70+: Layer-0 count-word neuron: fires on ' seven' and ' twelve' and nowhere else in the prompt (0.77 and 0.86). It marks both count slots, so the key after ' seven' and the query at ' twelve' share a 'count word' feature for the copy heads to match.
roles.L0/N883+: Layer-0 count-word neuron: fires on ' seven' and ' twelve' and nowhere else in the prompt (0.41 and 0.93). It marks both count slots, so the key after ' seven' and the query at ' twelve' share a 'count word' feature for the copy heads to match.
roles.L0/N1654+: Layer-0 neuron that fires on ' twelve' only (0.80): a second-count marker on the query position.
roles.L0/N1101+: Layer-0 time-unit neuron: fires on ' week' (2.8), ' days' (3.3) and ' year' (3.1). It writes 'time unit' into ' days', the value the copy heads move, and into ' year', the subject of the second clause.
roles.L0/N912+: Layer-0 time-unit neuron on ' week', ' days' and ' year' (1.0, 0.8, 1.1); same job as N1101.
roles.L0/N2008+: Layer-0 neuron on ' week' and ' days' (0.44, 0.61): part of the token identity of the copied unit.
roles.L0/N780+: Layer-0 neuron that fires on ' days' only (1.79): the copied token's own identity, which the copy heads read as their value.
roles.L0/H0: Broad layer-0 head that spreads over the whole prompt (no weight above 0.2) and writes the sentence context at each position; the late heads need it to read the frame.
roles.L0/H2: At ' twelve' it attends 0.65 to ' seven', so the query carries the first count word as well as the second.
roles.L1/H7: Spreads over ' days', ' and', ' a', ' year' and ' twelve' (0.13-0.27 each) and writes the clause context, time units included, into the last position's query.
roles.L2/H3: Nearest-noun copier: at ' twelve' it attends 0.63 to ' year', adding the time-unit subject of the second clause to the query.
roles.L3/N456+: Mid-layer count-word neuron: active on ' seven' (1.71) and ' twelve' (1.75) only; it re-marks the two count slots before the copy heads read them.
roles.L3/H1: Copy head: at ' twelve' it attends 0.92 to ' days', the token after the first count word, and moves it to the last position.
roles.L3/H3: Induction-style head: at ' twelve' it attends 0.25 to ' days' (the rest to the first token as a sink) and copies ' days'; the largest single head when patched from the 'hours' prompt.
roles.L4/H0: Attends to ' has' (0.41) and ' days' (0.20): late support that adds the frame and the copied unit.
roles.L4/H7: Copy head: attends 1.00 to ' days' and writes it toward the output.
roles.L5/H7: Attends 1.00 to ' twelve' itself, so the output position keeps its count-word reading and expects a counted noun.
roles.L5/N207+: Active at ' twelve' (1.06, mean 0.10). It writes against whitespace and layout tokens, which pushes the output toward a content word. It favours ' days' and ' months' equally, so it does not choose between them.
roles.L5/N1617+: Active at ' twelve' (1.17). It raises ' days' (+1.27) and ' months' (+1.22) about equally: a 'counted noun comes next' writer, not the chooser.
roles.L5/N1622+: A default-on neuron, above its corpus mean at ' twelve' (6.56 against 5.64). It is a generic output prior, part of what keeps the answer's log-probability high.
roles.L5/N822+: Count-word neuron at the output layer: active on ' seven' (2.26) and ' twelve' (2.46).
roles.L5/N2036-: Negative pole at ' twelve' (-0.11, corpus mean +0.13). Its output raises layout tokens, so keeping it below its mean keeps them down.
roles.L5/N575-: Negative pole at ' twelve' (-0.17, mean 0.0), which keeps the layout and byte tokens it writes down.
roles.L5/N119-: Negative pole at ' twelve' (-0.06, corpus mean +0.44). It writes whitespace tokens when on, so keeping it below its mean keeps them down.

claim.explanation: A copy route, not world knowledge. Layer-0 count-word neurons (N1877, N1277, N1108, N141, N70, N883, N1654) and L3/N456 mark ' seven' and ' twelve'. Time-unit neurons (N1101, N912, N2008, N780) write the identity of ' days', ' week' and ' year'. Early heads (L0/H0, L0/H2, L1/H7, L2/H3) build a query at ' twelve': 'a count word after <time unit> has'. Copy heads L3/H1, L3/H3 and L4/H7 (with L4/H0) match it to the token after the first count word and move ' days' to the last position, and L5/H7 keeps the count-word reading there. Layer-5 neurons (N207, N1617, N1622, N822 and the negative poles N2036, N575, N119) push the output toward a counted noun and away from layout tokens. They do not choose between ' days' and ' months', so the copied unit wins. The fact that a year has twelve months is weaker than this copy. Swap ' days' for another noun and the answer follows it; remove the noun and the route has nothing to copy.
claim.corrupted: A week has seven hours and a year has twelve

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has seven hours and a year has twelve
counterfactuals.why: Source swap of the copied noun: the copy heads move ' hours' from after ' seven' instead of ' days', so ' hours' is on top.

counterfactuals.prompt: A month has thirty days and a year has twelve
counterfactuals.why: Source swap that keeps the copied noun: ' thirty' is still a count word that the number neurons mark, and ' days' still follows it. So the copy heads still move ' days', and the wrong ' days' stays even though the subject changed.

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has 7 days and a year has twelve
counterfactuals.why: The first count is a digit, not a word, but ' days' still follows the count after ' has'. The copy is keyed on the noun's slot, so ' days' stays.

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has seven and a year has twelve
counterfactuals.why: The copied unit is removed from the first clause. Nothing follows ' seven' for the copy heads to move, so ' days' loses its source and is not the top token.

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has seven apples and a year has twelve
counterfactuals.why: The copied noun is not a time unit. The copy heads move ' apples', and with nothing to copy, ' days' falls; ' days' is not on top.

counterfactuals.prompt: A month has thirty days and a week has seven
counterfactuals.why: Here copying is right: the noun after the first count is ' days', so the copy route gives ' days', the correct answer.

counterfactuals.prompt: A spider has eight legs and a dog has four
counterfactuals.why: Here copying is right in another domain: the route copies ' legs' from after ' eight', so the top token is ' legs', not ' days'.

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has seven days, and a year has twelve
counterfactuals.why: A comma adds a token but leaves the 'count word, noun' slot and the 'has <count>' frame intact, so the copy heads still move ' days'.

prompts.prompt: A year has twelve months and a week has seven
prompts.why: Order swapped: the copied noun is now months, so the route should copy ' months', not ' days'.

prompts.prompt: A day has twenty-four hours and a week has seven
prompts.why: Copied noun is hours; the answer should follow it away from ' days'.

prompts.prompt: A decade has ten years and a century has one hundred
prompts.why: Different count words and unit; route should copy ' years'.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days while a year has twelve
prompts.why: Connective changed from 'and' to 'while'; copy of ' days' after the first count word should persist.

prompts.prompt: In one week there are seven days and in one year there are twelve
prompts.why: Paraphrased frame with the same source ' seven days' and query ' twelve'.

prompts.prompt: A fortnight has fourteen days and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Different first count word, same noun ' days' to copy.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days, a leap year has more, and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Distractor clause between source and query; copy heads should still reach ' days'.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve months and a decade has ten
prompts.why: The nearest count-then-noun is 'twelve months', so the copy should shift to ' months'.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve and a month has four
prompts.why: Third clause with a new count word; the route still copies ' days' as the only noun after a count word.

prompts.prompt: A tripod has three legs and a table has four
prompts.why: Non-time domain: copy route should give ' legs', not ' days'.

prompts.prompt: A chess team has seven days and a band has twelve
prompts.why: Odd frame, but the copy route on ' days' after ' seven' needs no world knowledge.

prompts.prompt: The week has seven days and the year has twelve
prompts.why: Determiners instead of 'a'; the copy route keys on count words and ' days'.

prompts.prompt: Seven days make a week and twelve
prompts.why: Noun precedes the count word, reversing the key adjacency; the route has no ' seven days' key at the expected position.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven. Days. A year has twelve
prompts.why: Sentence break between ' seven' and ' days' removes the adjacency the induction-style copy needs.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve and a week has seven
prompts.why: Repeated frame then final ' seven'; the route copies ' days' after the first ' seven'.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve months and a week has seven days and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Full repeat: ' twelve months' now exists earlier, so induction copy should give ' months', not ' days'.

prompts.prompt: Zorp has seven blicks and Zumm has twelve
prompts.why: Nonsense noun: the route copies ' blicks' (first token), not ' days'.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve, and a month has thirty
prompts.why: Longer prompt with an added count query; the route still copies ' days'.

prompts.prompt: Q: How many days are in a week? A: seven. Q: How many months are in a year? A: twelve
prompts.why: No ' seven days' adjacency; Q/A format with months named in the question, so the route has nothing to copy to ' days'.

prompts.prompt: Un semaine a sept jours et une annee a douze
prompts.why: French: layer-0 count-word neurons key on English tokens, so the route should not carry ' days'.
